scope: Instrumented diagnostic on one shared host, no intentional faults. Not a production correction, SLO, capacity guarantee or operational acceptance.
overall_rationale: No mandatory gate failed. One resource gate in DS2-r1 (file-descriptor persistence) is NOT VERIFIED under the frozen policy.

environment.image: disposable flat image from original Level 7 + ten hash-locked wheels (--no-index --no-deps --require-hashes) + six modules from git show HEAD; pip check clean; package diff exactly ten additions; generator layer adds httpx 0.28.1

environment.mounts: no training data or holdout in benchmark containers

plan.per_run: fresh service container; wait for health and first successful explanation (also DS0); reference explanation; bounded drain by the committed generator; no repetition discarded or replaced; at most 8 primaries
plan.cohorts: by arrival number k: warm-up k < rate*10; measurement rate*10 <= k < rate*70; whole run all. Time series: 12 half-open 5 s measurement windows [t_start+10+5i, +5); requests by arrival number, timestamped events and samples by monotonic time in [a,b)
plan.latency: actual task start to terminal; linear-interpolation percentiles; prediction degradation uses all-terminal measurement p95
plan.baseline: arithmetic mean of DS0-r1 and DS0-r2 measurement prediction p95; invalid if either DS0 has invalid generator scheduling or non-100% prediction success; no historical substitute
plan.generator_gates: per active class: 0 missed; scheduling-lag p99 <= 10 ms in measurement AND whole run; reconciliation; plus 0 outstanding after drain and no unexpected generator error
plan.generator_validity_rule: if any generator gate fails: the gate stays FAIL; performance-attribution gates (prediction p95 degradation, explanation success >= 95%, explanation p95 <= 150 ms) become NOT VERIFIED with the observed numeric result kept; direct observations (success/contract/association, unexpected errors, restarts, lifecycle, resources) keep PASS/FAIL; no window is salvaged as an acceptance pass; a run with a failed gate cannot be PASS
prediction_gates: DS1/DS2: p95 degradation <= max(20% baseline, 5 ms)
plan.DS0: idle worker stable: one generation, one pid, no failure; explanation performance gates NOT APPLICABLE
plan.unexpected_failure: committed recovery runs unaided; lifecycle and post-recovery responses recorded; recovery NOT VERIFIED if no later success is observed
plan.resource_gates: memory peak <= 90% of 1 GiB; 0 OOM. Observation: drain, 15 s idle, snapshot, one GET /health, 2 s, snapshot, then one explanation check. fds <= post-ready and threads <= post-ready (+2 parent) at the final snapshot is PASS; otherwise NOT VERIFIED (persistence not established), except parent threads > post-ready+40 is FAIL. Exactly one worker, no unresolved job. Clean shutdown: exit 0, not OOM-killed, shutdown complete, dispatcher stopped, cleanup and terminations confirmed, no worker left, no tracker leak warning, no Traceback
plan.overall: PASS only if every applicable gate passes in all 8; any FAIL gives FAIL; else any NOT VERIFIED gives NOT VERIFIED

anomaly_flags_descriptive_only.worker_process_cpu_over_25ms: process CPU over the handle interval of any request starting in the window
anomaly_flags_descriptive_only.queue_at_limit: queued 8 at an admission/rejection event or sample

plan.anomaly_comparison: each flagged window against the nearest unflagged window on each side within the same run; condition-level flagged vs unflagged medians. Descriptive only; temporal association is not causation. Periodic samples are not continuous state
plan.worker_timing_definition: engine = ExplanationEngine.explain; handle = WorkerCore.handle_explain; cycle = frame decoded to reply frame written (excludes parent queue and request-pipe transit); thread CPU = worker main thread; process CPU = all worker threads; run-queue wait = main-thread schedstat wait over handle
plan.clock: service, worker and generator share the VM CLOCK_MONOTONIC (same boot_id, zero timens offsets). Host monotonic mapped by minimum-RTT ping-pong over a docker exec stream before and after each run (offset before is used); drift and RTT recorded
plan.instrumentation: identical for all 8: scratch probe wrapper, 100 ms in-process sampler, worker timers, generator shim (10 ms loop-lag probe replacing the committed one with the same cadence, 100 ms CPU record), 1 s host sampler (process table every 2 s, thermal/memory every 5 s). No public endpoint, no host configuration change, no privilege

overhead_check.design: one pair, DS2 rates, 5 s warm-up + 20 s measurement; plain arm = committed app, committed generator loop monitor, no probe, sampler or worker timers (host sampler running in both)
overhead_check.reading: Container CPU differed by 0.4%. The instrumented arm had higher explanation latency (p50 +2.9 ms, p95 +9.0 ms) and a longer prediction tail (p99 +3.9 ms). One unreplicated pair cannot separate overhead from run-to-run variation; equivalence is not claimed.

clock.uncertainty: minimum round trip about 1 ms; host-VM drift within each run below 0.1 ms. Host samples are 1-6 s apart, so host window figures are coarse.

observed_anomalies: No execution timeout, rejection, restart, worker failure, missed arrival, or queue at limit in any primary run. Maximum queued: 1 (DS1), 2-5 (DS2).

Per-explanation CPU time rose without any fault in DS1-r2: windows 8-11 had mean worker thread CPU 21.1-23.8 ms against about 19-20 ms earlier in that run. Those windows also showed 3.3-3.7 busy host logical CPUs (DS1 median 1.8), 1.1-1.5 cores in the 'other' host process category (median 0.28) and swap-ins. No DS2 window had a comparable rise (all window means 15.6-16.7 ms).
In every mixed-load run, per-explanation CPU time was higher at 20/s (run means 18.4 and 20.3 ms) than at 40/s (15.8-16.3 ms).

Isolated generator arrivals more than 10 ms late occurred in several windows of every condition, including DS0, without breaching the p99 validity gate. Flagged windows had higher median prediction maxima (about 35-38 ms against 14-17 ms) with similar p95.
Besides a start-up stall in every run, six of eight runs had one generator loop stall over 20 ms at about 6,170-6,230 scheduled arrivals: 44 s at 140/s, 52 s at 120/s, 62 s at 100/s.

DS2-r1: parent file descriptors were 16 after readiness, after drain and after 15 s idle, and 17 in the final snapshot taken after the health probe. DS2-r4 showed 17 at readiness. The gate is NOT VERIFIED as predeclared.

comparison_with_earlier_milestones.L8-2D_P2_r3: No defining symptom occurred (no multi-second prediction stall, missed arrivals, deadline error or replacement). Not reproduced.
comparison_with_earlier_milestones.L8-2DF_DF1-r1: No sustained cost rise to saturation. The largest window mean here was 23.8 ms thread CPU (at 20/s); at 40/s it was 16.7 ms. DF1-r1's about 28 ms was CPU ticks divided by completions, a different measure, so the figures are not directly comparable.
comparison_with_earlier_milestones.L8-2DF_DF2-r1: No uninjected execution timeout and no generator-invalid run. The cause of that run's events remains unknown.

confirmed_findings: All 56,000 scheduled predictions and 14,000 scheduled explanations succeeded in eight fault-free runs, with no missed arrivals, contract or association violations.
All eight generators met the frozen validity gates.
Prediction p95 stayed within the allowance: DS0 mean 8.11 ms; DS1 9.19 and 10.30 ms; DS2 7.33-7.63 ms.
Successful explanation p95: DS1 37.0 and 45.8 ms; DS2 33.9-35.6 ms.
Worker busy fraction (frame decoded to reply written; excludes parent dispatch and request-pipe time) was 0.44-0.48 at 20/s and 0.76-0.78 at 40/s (5 s window maximum 0.80).

Worker elapsed time exceeded CPU time by about 3 ms on average (CPU/elapsed 0.84-0.86). After subtracting main-thread run-queue wait the median remainder was about -0.1 ms (measurement skew), so the gap was time waiting to run, not time blocked.
No container CPU throttling occurred in any measurement window; peak memory was about 42% of the limit with no OOM; shutdowns were clean.
plausible_mechanisms_not_established: Competing host demand and host memory swapping reducing effective CPU speed may explain DS1-r2's late cost rise. This is co-occurrence in one run. Rank correlations pool autocorrelated windows, and Docker VM and total host CPU include the worker's own consumption, so they are partly circular.
Higher per-request cost at the lower rate may reflect CPU wake-up, frequency or cache effects at low duty cycle. Frequency was not measurable.
A request-count-driven event in the generator process, for example a full garbage collection, may explain the repeated stall position. Garbage collection was not instrumented.
At 40/s arrivals are 25 ms apart and the mean worker cycle was about 19-20 ms; arithmetically a sustained rise of roughly 25-30% would leave no idle time. This is not a capacity guarantee.
unresolved: Initiating cause of P2_r3, of DF1-r1's cost rise and of DF2-r1's events.
Incidence of rare events: eight repetitions cannot estimate it.
Why DS0 prediction p50 (6.4 ms) was higher than under mixed load (4.0-5.1 ms).
What the 'other' host process demand was (process names were deliberately not retained).
Holdout historical non-access and content preservation: NOT VERIFIED (unchanged).
limitations: One shared host, instrumented execution, overhead not isolated.
Host telemetry is coarse and has no actual frequency or hypervisor scheduling data.
Fixed run order; conditions are not randomised and host conditions varied between runs.
DS0 and DS1 have two repetitions each.
Worker timers exclude parent-side queueing and request-pipe transit.
Periodic samples do not establish continuous state.

existing_archive_verification.DS2_r1_descriptor_records: The inspected run record holds counts only: parent 16 post-ready, 16 post-drain, 16 pre-probe, 17 post-probe; no identity, connection state or later observation. interpretation_clarifications: CPU figures cover the worker main thread. The measured handler includes response conversion and validation.

Elapsed minus CPU time is not by itself proof of scheduling wait. The original attribution also used per-request main-thread schedstat run-queue wait over the same handler, leaving a median remainder of about -0.1 ms. That supports it in aggregate for those runs; it does not establish it for every request or say why the thread waited.
DF1-r1 CPU-cost estimates used a different measure and are not directly comparable.
Higher CPU cost at moderate load is an observation, not a proven frequency or cache effect.
Correlations with host activity and swapping do not establish causation.
The stall pattern near 6,200 scheduled requests does not establish garbage collection as its cause.
Worker occupancy sensitivity arithmetic is illustrative, not a capacity guarantee.

The omitted flagged-versus-normal comparison, the separate supplementary analysis, the exploratory occupancy, rank-correlation and stall-position analyses, the instrumentation-overhead limits and the poorly discriminating 25 ms CPU flag stand as originally recorded.
l8_2dsv_reconciliation.original_descriptor_observer_effect_limi: L8-2DS descriptor snapshots were collected through a temporary HTTP route inside the measured service, so each monitoring request could have contributed its own connection descriptor (and in-process listing can include its own directory descriptor). This does not establish the identity of DS2-r1's additional descriptor, and its gate remains NOT VERIFIED.

plan.fd_rule: per role. residual = identities at a cycle's probe+15 not in baseline. FAIL if final counts strictly grow baseline<c1<c2, or a residual class count grows c1->c2, or the same residual socket persists across both cycle ends. PASS if no residual, or identical residual identities at both ends all of class pipe/eventpoll/eventfd/dev-null/app file. Otherwise NOT VERIFIED. Any missing snapshot NOT VERIFIED. frozen_follow_up.post_freeze_description_correction: The plan calls readiness HTTP health polling. The committed ready mode polls /health and then posts explanations until one succeeds, before the idle wait and baseline. Hence one extra admitted explanation per lifetime (2001) and the startup explanation_unavailable rejections. No rule, tool or workload changed.

request_accounting_successful.excluded: readiness requests and one health probe per cycle

l8_2dsv_reconciliation.finding: In all 34 snapshot rows analyzed per role (baseline plus 16 per lifetime, two lifetimes) the parent held 14 descriptors and the explanation worker 9. No descriptor identity outside the baseline was observed and none was missing at either cycle end. No persistent or monotonic accumulation was observed.
observation_limits: Discrete snapshots; descriptors that opened and closed between them are not seen, and none were taken during traffic.

No connection socket appeared in any analyzed snapshot, including those right after drain and right after the probe; health connections lasted about 2-3 ms and were closed by the client. There was no positive control showing the observer catching an open connection; it did classify the listening TCP socket.

The observer ran by docker exec as the image default user (uid 0 in the container, same user as the service), with no privileged mode or added capability. It shares the service cgroup, so it adds some CPU and memory use.
The observer was not smoke-tested separately before the primaries.
Two short lifetimes; they do not establish behavior over long runs or rare events.
Counts here are not directly comparable with L8-2DS counts: both wrapper and observation method differ.

limits: Overlap in time is not causation; the overlap script was written after results.
No generator generation-2 collection was recorded in any cycle; the longest recorded generator pause (about 3.2 ms) is far shorter than the worst arrival lag (about 35-40 ms).
No recorded service-parent collection overlapped a late arrival; the worker was not instrumented.
Cycles are too short to reach the historical position near 6,200 requests; its absence does not show the earlier stalls are resolved.
gc callbacks add a small unmeasured overhead; thresholds were not changed and no collection was forced.

other_limitations: Instrumented execution on one shared host; overhead not measured in this follow-up.
Lag p99 was gated separately for each warm-up and measurement window.
Generator image installs httpx 0.28.1 as before; its transitive dependencies are not hash-locked.
